completion_data.completion_summary: Implemented hooks/validate-bounded-waiter.sh, a PreToolUse Bash hook that blocks a loop+sleep+process-name-match conjunction (pgrep/ps|grep self-match waiters), with a 23-case fixture suite, a bare registration in merge-sources/settings-hooks.json, and manifest wiring. Deployed, live-fired, and verified end-to-end via a real Bash tool call. Phase 4 closed COMPLETED WITH EXCLUSIONS: verify-deploy.sh showed 33/36 passing, with all 3 failures investigated and confirmed pre-existing and unrelated to this task's deliverables.

memory_candidates.content: A PreToolUse hook that must text-match a wait-loop self-match shape (loop keyword + sleep + process-name test) should match the name-match test as a BARE WORD (e.g. `pgrep` with any flags or none) rather than narrowing to a specific flag. When the match is already gated by a conjunction of multiple independent legs (loop + sleep + name-test), the conjunction itself supplies the false-positive safety, so a bare-word leg closes every flag-clustering evasion (-af, -fa, -x -f, --full, no flags) by construction instead of requiring an enumerated, driftable flag list kept current by hand. Pin this with dedicated flag-clustering fixture cases so a future narrowing regresses loudly.

update-task-status.sh's --file-scope-add flag is restricted to operation=postflight with target_status in {research, plan} -- it hard-errors for any other operation/target_status combination, including implement. A dispatch instruction describing it as 'the sanctioned mid-run re-scope path' during an implement-phase dispatch is incorrect as stated; there is currently no sanctioned implement-time file_scope-widening entry point. When a plan assumes this mechanism is available mid-implement, verify it first rather than attempting the call, and if it fails as expected, decline the dependent edit and record the mechanical finding rather than hand-editing specs/state.json's file_scope array to work around it.

Once a write-time PreToolUse Bash-matcher hook is deployed and live for the current session, hand-driving further fixture-style test commands DIRECTLY through the Bash tool (e.g. `jq -n --arg c "<banned-shape-text>" ... | bash hook.sh`) can trip that same hook on the OUTER Bash tool call's own raw command text, even though the banned text is only a quoted jq argument intended as synthetic test data -- the hook does text-level matching on the whole command string, not shell-aware parsing of argument boundaries. Workaround: write the test-driver logic to a file via the Write tool (never a Bash heredoc, which has the same problem) and invoke it with a short, pattern-free `bash /path/to/script.sh` Bash tool call instead.
